names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 13 martie, «Sfânta Muceniță Hristina din Persia».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 13 Μαρτίου, «Αγία Χριστίνα η εν Περσία», with the rank words left off.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's second heading for the Julian 13 March on pravoslavno.rs, „Света мученица Христина Персијанка.“, with Света left off, which is not a rank, and with the rank word мученица left off. Персијанка is kept: it is not a rank but the epithet the heading itself gives her, and it is what this folder's English name already carries.
Read out of the name link behind days.pravoslavie.ru's line for 13 марта ст. ст., «Христина Персидская, мц.», with the rank word left off. The day's own line gives the same form, declined.

death.note: doxologia.ro: «ea a fost torturată cu cruzime în Persia, în veacul al patrulea». The page gives no year.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 13 марта ст. ст. — «Мц. Христины Персидской (IV).»

attestations.note: The fourth century the line closes with is the century this folder already held from the Romanian and Serbian calendars, so the interval is unchanged. The reading behind the line is one sentence and adds no place in Persia, no persecutor and no year. The day page prints no hymn under her name.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 13 martie — «Sfânta Muceniță Hristina din Persia»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 13ης Μαρτίου — «Αγία Χριστίνα η εν Περσία»

attestations.note: The page holds one sentence, «Η Αγία Χριστίνα η εν Περσία μαρτύρησε αφού την μαστίγωσαν μέχρι θανάτου», and two lines of verse; it gives no year, no persecutor and no hymn, and the corpus's fourth-century interval stands as it was.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 26.03.2026 (13. март ст. ст.) — „Света мученица Христина Персијанка.“

attestations.note: The day's second entry, of three. Its four sentences say what the Romanian and Greek pages already said and nothing more: that she was cruelly tortured in Persia in the fourth century for the unshaken confession of the faith of Christ, that her torturers scourged her with whips until she grew weak and died, and that her soul parted from her tortured body and entered the eternal joy of Christ the King and Lord. The century agrees with the interval this folder already holds, so no date was touched; the entry gives no year, no city in Persia and no persecutor. The stored Serbian form keeps Персијанка, which is not a rank but the epithet that tells her from the other Christinas, and leaves off Света мученица. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.
